title: Rpg maker making new characters on KRITA (help).

posts.author: tzartos
posts.body: I was in need of a drawing program because i think that is the only way to make new enemies in rpg maker. I saw some videos and end up downloading KRITA as the program to draw in some of my enemies and characters of my game. I would like to know the Width - Height - Resolution that an image needs to be imported  afterwards in RPG MAKER without any problems... i mean you cant just do any resolution you like it makes no sence... it probably needs spacific image size or a spacific PREDEFINED that gives fixed sizes of all 3 (Width - Height - Resolution). Has anyone else tryed KRITA? is it a good choice for drawing enemies and characters?? Is it easy to export and import on rpg maker afterwards? i really have many questions cause i just found out i have to draw a lot and never tried before. Thanks for reading.

posts.author: Big_D
posts.body:
Krita is really good, and yeah it's pretty easy to import and export into RPGM. But the resolution does need to match its actual size ingame. The default RPGM game resolution is 816x624 but can be modified in the Community_Basic plugin, I think 1280x720 is a decent and common upgrade from that, the work involved sort of scales exponentially.
To use the drawings ingame, export your Krita file as a .png and save it inside Documents/Games/[your game]/img/[the relevant folder]. If you save it in pictures, you can use it with Show Picture. If you save it in Parallaxes, it comes up as a Parallax background, etc. If you need to update a piece of art after using it already, just save over the same file in the img folder, it'll automatically adjust it ingame too.
